findings.highlight: There’s no room for me to question her about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の意思には疑問を挟む余地などない。
findings.governingReading: Saber’s stated will admits no doubt or challenge.
findings.explanation: The English says Shirou has no opportunity to ask her about the matter, changing certainty in Saber’s resolve into a conversational restriction.

findings.highlight: we Servants, who are also spirits.
findings.evidenceJa: 同じ霊格を持つサーヴァントだけです。
findings.governingReading: Only Servants, who possess the same spiritual rank or order as the Grail, can touch it.
findings.explanation: The English preserves incorporeal similarity but deletes equal 霊格, the ontological rank that explains compatibility with the Grail.

findings.highlight: Saber has a wish she wants granted.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーにも“叶えるべき願い”があるって事だ。
findings.governingReading: Saber too has a wish that is to be fulfilled—one she regards as requiring fulfillment.
findings.explanation: “Wants granted” weakens べき’s obligation or necessity into ordinary desire, blunting the reason Shirou sees no hesitation in her.

findings.highlight: you will have to use one of your Command Spells to compensate for treading inside me.
findings.evidenceJa: 私に踏みいる代償として、その刻印を一つ頂く事になりますが
findings.governingReading: As the price of trespassing upon Saber’s inviolable self or principles, Shirou would forfeit one Command Spell.
findings.explanation: “Treading inside me” copies the Japanese spatial metaphor into non-English wording and obscures that an order violating her principles requires coercion through a Command Spell.

findings.highlight: Her lack of doubt gave her the image of a cold fighting machine
findings.evidenceJa: あまりの強さと迷いのなさに機械のようなイメージがあったけど
findings.governingReading: Her overwhelming strength together with her total lack of hesitation had made her seem machine-like to Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English omits her extraordinary strength as half the basis of the image and adds “cold fighting,” turning a broad machine impression into a stock killer-machine characterization.

findings.highlight: Oh, sorry, I apologized without realizing it.
findings.evidenceJa: ああ、思わず謝ってた
findings.governingReading: Shirou realizes that he had instinctively found himself apologizing.
findings.explanation: The inserted “sorry” makes him apologize again while explaining the first apology; 思わず describes its involuntary emergence, not failure to notice that it happened.

findings.highlight: beings that have reached the rank of gods
findings.evidenceJa: 神域まで上り詰めた存在です
findings.governingReading: They are beings who, by individual power, climbed as far as the divine domain.
findings.explanation: The English promotes reaching the realm of the divine into attaining the rank of gods, overstating Servants’ ontological status.

findings.highlight: heroes that had supernatural abilities while they were alive
findings.evidenceJa: 生前に卓越した能力を持った英雄
findings.governingReading: Heroic spirits are heroes who possessed outstanding ability in life.
findings.explanation: “Supernatural” changes exceptional excellence into paranormal power, excluding historically human forms of heroism allowed by the source definition.

findings.highlight: If our weaknesses are revealed, the enemy will take advantage of them to defeat us.
findings.evidenceJa: 弱点を知られれば、まず間違いなくそこを突かれ、敗北する
findings.governingReading: If a weakness becomes known, the enemy will almost certainly exploit it and cause defeat.
findings.explanation: The English removes まず間違いなく’s explicitly high but nonabsolute probability and states the defeat as an unqualified result.

findings.highlight: Summoning a true heroic spirit
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊をまるごと召喚する
findings.governingReading: Summoning a heroic spirit in its entirety is itself nearly miraculous.
findings.explanation: “True heroic spirit” changes completeness of the summoned entity into genuineness, obscuring why the Grail uses class vessels to limit the manifestation.

findings.highlight: Those are the seven classes.
findings.evidenceJa: この世界に我々が存在できる依り代を用意したのです。
findings.governingReading: The Grail prepared anchors or vessels through which the Servants can exist in this world.
findings.explanation: mirror moon omits the entire active sentence explaining the class vessels’ function as worldly anchors, then jumps directly to naming the seven classes.

findings.highlight: if your enemy is stronger than you in combat
findings.evidenceJa: 敵が自身より白兵戦で優れている場合
findings.governingReading: Saber asks what Shirou would do if an enemy surpassed him specifically in close-quarters combat.
findings.explanation: “Combat” broadens 白兵戦 from melee to all forms of fighting, weakening the tactical premise that another method can bypass close-combat superiority.

findings.highlight: all you have to do is beat them some other way.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣以外で敵の息の根を絶つだけの話じゃないか。
findings.governingReading: If the sword cannot prevail, one simply ends the enemy’s life by some other means.
findings.explanation: “Beat them” euphemizes 息の根を絶つ, explicitly killing or stopping the enemy’s breath, softening the severity of Shirou’s tactical realization.

findings.highlight:
has
 an
 a special
 ability to hide its presence
findings.evidenceJa: 能力こそ低いですが気配を隠すという能力がありますし
findings.governingReading: Although Assassin’s raw capabilities are low, the class possesses the ability to conceal its presence.
findings.explanation: The displayed English contains unreconciled alternatives—“an / a special”—and therefore leaves a grammatically broken line in a central class explanation.

findings.highlight: as heroic spirits, we have our guaranteed fatal attack.
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊である以上は必殺の機会を持っているのです
findings.governingReading: Every Servant, by virtue of being a heroic spirit, possesses an opportunity or means to produce a decisive kill.
findings.explanation: The English turns possession of a lethal opportunity into ownership of a guaranteed fatal attack, overstating certainty and making 宝具 sound like an automatic hit.

findings.highlight: Heroes have the weapons that symbolize them and make them a hero.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らはシンボルとなる武具を持つが故に、英雄として特化している
findings.governingReading: Because they possess armaments that serve as their symbols, these figures are crystallized or specialized as heroes.
findings.explanation: “Make them a hero” collapses the source’s reciprocal mechanism between legend and symbolic armament into a generic qualification for herohood.

findings.highlight: I recall that blue knight.
findings.evidenceJa: あの青い騎士の槍を思い出す。
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls the lance belonging to the blue knight.
findings.explanation: The English changes the remembered object from Lancer’s weapon to Lancer himself, disrupting the transition into analysis of the lance as a Noble Phantasm.

findings.highlight: The lance that absorbed magical energy from the air and pierced Saber’s chest with incredible movements.
findings.evidenceJa: あり得ない軌跡でセイバーの胸を貫いたあの槍。
findings.governingReading: The lance pierced Saber’s chest along an impossible trajectory.
findings.explanation: “Incredible movements” is an awkward plural animation of the weapon and loses the precise impossibility of its path through causality.

findings.highlight: the lance itself wasn’t extraordinary.
findings.evidenceJa: それ自体は槍っていう領域から出てなかっただろ。
findings.governingReading: Before its true-name release, the weapon itself had not departed from the category or bounds of a lance.
findings.explanation: “Wasn’t extraordinary” says it lacked exceptional quality, while the source says that however ominous it was, it remained categorically a spear until activation.

findings.highlight: In exchange for revealing the name
findings.evidenceJa: 正体を明かすかわりに
findings.governingReading: In exchange for revealing the Servant’s identity, the Noble Phantasm unleashes its unavoidable decisive blow.
findings.explanation: The English narrows 正体, the hero’s identity exposed through the weapon name, to merely revealing a name.

findings.highlight: the Servant will expose all its weaknesses.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの欠点をもさらけ出す事になる。
findings.governingReading: If the trump card fails, the Servant will have exposed their own weakness as well as their identity.
findings.explanation: The English adds “all,” overstating a revealed exploitable flaw as disclosure of every weakness the Servant has.

findings.highlight: Servants themselves are powerful magic.
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントはそれ自体が強力な魔力ですから。
findings.governingReading: A Servant is, in itself, a powerful concentration or body of magical energy.
findings.explanation: “Powerful magic” changes the Servant’s detectable energetic constitution into a spell or supernatural practice, weakening the mechanism of presence sensing.

findings.highlight: I sigh.
findings.evidenceJa: はあ、と肩で息をつく。
findings.governingReading: Shirou exhales while breathing visibly through his shoulders, physically showing his discouragement or exertion.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the exhalation but removes the shoulder movement and heavier breathing encoded by 肩で息をつく.

findings.highlight: close your eyes and breathe normally.
findings.evidenceJa: 目を閉じて呼吸を整えてください
findings.governingReading: Saber instructs Shirou to close his eyes and deliberately regulate or steady his breathing.
findings.explanation: “Breathe normally” replaces an active preparatory adjustment with maintaining an ordinary state, weakening the meditative procedure.

findings.highlight: Could this be the end of her sword
findings.evidenceJa: これってまさか刃物の先か
findings.governingReading: Could the prickling object possibly be the point of some blade?
findings.explanation: The English specifies Saber’s sword before Shirou knows the object and says “end” rather than a blade point; the next page reveals it is her fingertip, so the added identification misdirects the physical action.

findings.highlight: They are the calm eyes of a swordsman who allows no disagreement.
findings.evidenceJa: 否定を許さない、冷徹な剣士の目だ。
findings.governingReading: Her narrowed eyes are those of a cold, implacable swordsman who will permit no denial.
findings.explanation: “Calm” removes 冷徹’s severity and emotional hardness, softening Saber’s coercive pressure at the first major clash of their goals.

findings.highlight: I stare back, trying not to lose
findings.evidenceJa: それに気圧されまいと視線を返して
findings.governingReading: Shirou returns her gaze so as not to be overawed or cowed by it.
findings.explanation: “Trying not to lose” invents a competitive outcome and obscures that he is resisting the pressure of Saber’s gaze before stating his policy.

findings.highlight: I know I can’t survive this without doing anything.
findings.evidenceJa: 無傷で、何もしないままじゃ生き残れないって事は判ってる
findings.governingReading: Shirou knows he cannot survive both unscathed and without taking action.
findings.explanation: The English omits 無傷で, making him claim he cannot survive at all if inactive rather than conceding that survival without injury and action is impossible.

findings.highlight: you are fighting
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師として避けられない戦い
findings.governingReading: Saber frames this as a battle Shirou cannot avoid in his capacity as a magus.
findings.explanation: The English omits the entire magus-specific inevitability, weakening her premise that participation follows from his identity before contrasting their goals.

findings.highlight: I don’t feel anything toward the Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯なんて言われても実感が湧かない。
findings.governingReading: Even when told of the Grail, Shirou cannot form a concrete, lived sense of its reality or value.
findings.explanation: “Don’t feel anything toward” turns lack of experiential reality into emotional indifference, flattening why an abstract prize cannot motivate him.

findings.highlight: not to involve any unnecessary people.
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係な人を巻き込まないように
findings.governingReading: Shirou will do everything he can to avoid involving people unrelated to the war.
findings.explanation: “Unnecessary people” categorizes human beings as superfluous rather than innocent of involvement, producing unnatural English and distorting his protective principle.

findings.highlight: it’s only an opinion that I received from my father
findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣の受け売りなんだけどな
findings.governingReading: Shirou admits he is parroting or borrowing the maxim from Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: “An opinion that I received” is nonidiomatic and loses 受け売り’s self-aware admission that the wording and idea are secondhand, an important marker of Shirou’s inherited ideal.

findings.highlight: I should be selfish to become a superhero.
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方になるんだったらエゴイストになれ
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu told him that if he meant to become an ally of justice, he must become an egoist.
findings.explanation: “Superhero” imports a genre identity and public costumed-hero frame into 正義の味方, changing the work’s recurring ethical ideal and its paradoxical instruction.

findings.highlight: A Noble Phantasm could be called a materialized divine mystery.
findings.evidenceJa: 宝具とは、ある意味カタチになった神秘ですから。
findings.governingReading: A Noble Phantasm is, in a sense, mystery given form.
findings.explanation: “Divine” adds a religious/divine qualification to 神秘 (“mystery”), which is the broader Fate concept of mystery/arcane power.

findings.highlight: As spells are necessary to activate magic, recitation of the true name is necessary to awaken and to activate the Noble Phantasm.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術の発現に詠唱が必要なように、宝具の発動にも詠唱[line3][ruby text=しんめい char=2]真名による覚醒が必要になる。
findings.governingReading: Just as an incantation is needed for magecraft to manifest, a Noble Phantasm needs an invocation—awakening through the true name—to activate.
findings.explanation: The English changes 魔術 to generic “magic,” renders 詠唱 (“incantation”) as “spells,” and repeats “activate” awkwardly while obscuring the parallel between incantation and true-name invocation.
